is_anopheles.evidence: Studies Anopheles gambiae s.s. and Anopheles melas collected on Bioko Island, Equatorial Guinea (page 1, Abstract; page 5, Table 2).

reports_target_markers.evidence: Mosquitoes were screened for Vgsc L1014F (L995F), L1014S (L995S), and ace-1R (G119S/G280S) using real-time TaqMan assays (page 5, 'Specimen handling and molecular analyses'; page 8, 'Insecticide resistance').

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 4 (page 11) presents exact sample sizes and genotype counts (S/S, S/R, R/R) as well as L1014F allele frequencies for An. gambiae s.s. from Mongola, Arena Blanca, and Riaba. Table 3 (page 11) reports L1014F frequencies from light trap collections across multiple sites.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in the field across multiple sites on Bioko Island, Equatorial Guinea, during 2009 using HLC and LTC (page 3, 'Mosquito collections').

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary research article reporting original entomological data collected in 2009 on Bioko Island.

sub_country_location.evidence: Data are reported by specific sentinel locations on Bioko Island: Punta Europa (Mongola, Biabia, Cacahual), Riaba, Basacato del Oeste, Santa Maria, Arena Blanca, Bilelipa, Semu, and Bakake Grande (page 5, Table 1; page 11, Table 3 and Table 4).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: All collections took place during a single year, between February and December 2009 (page 3, 'Mosquito collections').

duplicate_risk.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in 2009 as part of routine BIMCP entomological monitoring; while biting rates for one site were previously mentioned in Reddy et al. 2011, this is the primary presentation of the comprehensive 2009 insecticide resistance data.

supplement.evidence: All relevant genotype counts and frequencies are reported directly in the main text in Tables 3 and 4.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated entomological transmission indicators and insecticide resistance alleles (Vgsc L1014F, L1014S, and Ace-1 G119S) on Bioko Island, Equatorial Guinea, in 2009. Only Vgsc L1014F was detected in An. gambiae s.s. (M molecular form), with full genotype counts (S/S, S/R, R/R) and allele frequencies provided for three sites from human landing collections, and allele frequencies from light trap collections across multiple sites.
